scope: Historical world_changes consumer coverage and explicit world-record foreign-key propagation
isolation: All behavioral checks used temporary synthetic books with fixture cleanup; no real manuscript, installation, or release was changed.
implementation: Normalize entity/rule dependency aliases to world.entities/world.rules for impact traversal.
Compare normalized world record values so actual definition/author-plan changes expand scope, while equivalent defaults, repeated links, and no-op record submissions do not.

Track expanded world seeds through update and refresh; synchronize heads, body hashes, reasons, required state, fences, and world review requirements; invalidate existing chapter and semantic reviews when new chapters enter.

Block legacy candidates at publication if their saved world changes have uncovered consumers; allow missing-plan recovery through plan, refresh, and resubmitted update without bypassing existing SHA/head/fence checks.

Traverse source chapters, active chapter-evidence records, explicit fact-to-knowledge/rule_requires relations, and declared chapter consumers through one typed queue; exclude retired record relations and fence reached records.

Retain actually changed world IDs in publication receipts so later same-target branches recover alias and transitive consumers; unchanged and merely revalidated records are not attached as new target outputs.
Preserve prepublication consumed dependency hashes. Changed direct world dependencies invalidate derived evidence caches; no hash is automatically replaced to claim a new read.

red_evidence.stage: Original world scope defect before implementation
red_evidence.observed: Changed entities and author-plan rules left consumers outside affected scope; legacy candidates could publish without consumer review.

red_evidence.stage: Additional explicit world-reference boundary before typed relation closure
red_evidence.observed: Changed author-plan fact returned affected=[1] instead of [1,2,3] for observed rule/knowledge dependents, or [1,3] for author-plan intermediates with formal consumers; retired relationship control passed.

coverage: entity/rule alias equivalence, canonical consumers, transitive chapters, independent chapter exclusion
actual publication updates consumer heads and retains original consumed hashes
same-target future branch preserves complete consumer range
normalized no-op world update does not expand or falsely record target production
changed direct and indirect fences reject refresh without writes
restoring an already expanded world candidate does not silently shrink review range
legacy saved patch publication guard and empty-update recovery
legacy patch plus imported consumer missing a plan recovers through plan/refresh/update
candidate chapter evidence and same-batch new entity remain stageable and publishable
insufficient response budget rolls back patch, scope, revision, and database
author-plan fact to observed or author-plan rule/knowledge reaches formal consumers
source body to observed fact to author-plan rule/knowledge reaches formal consumers
retired world relationship does not expand the branch

pagination_compatibility_followup.trigger: Parent full-suite validation reported that the existing 4000-chapter pagination test saw hints.total=8000 instead of 4000 after source observations were newly added as traversal hints.
pagination_compatibility_followup.fix: Keep typed traversal and all fences. Do not add source observations already present in world_review_required as extra traversal hints; preserve existing declared hints and new entity/author-plan/indirect-record hints.

validation.added_assertions: Source fact stays fenced without a duplicate hint; indirect author-plan rule and entity/rule change hints remain present.

limitations: Impact traversal follows recorded identifiers, evidence, receipts, and foreign keys; unrecorded semantic relationships remain author review responsibilities.
Dependency completeness remains an author declaration. Old consumed hashes are preserved even when a reviewed world mutation makes those cache keys stale.
